```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B is pure software. Browser-based link rooms are a mechanic the brief shows already works (JoinByKey). That suits one person with AI agents. A's hard parts are physical logistics (sourcing, warehousing, customs, breakage, address failures), and A's own brief concedes agents don't solve these.",
    "B's pricing anchors show a self-serve, low-ticket tier that small buyers already pay for: CrankWheel Solo at $29/mo and Blitzz at $15-19/agent/mo. That fits a fast first sale. A's brief says the category sells on enterprise terms ($15k-$20k+/yr Sendoso), which is a poor fit for closing a first customer within 90 days.",
    "B's demand evidence is thin but concrete. It cites three sourced first-person quotes describing the exact pain, including a complaint that the free incumbent, Quick Assist, is unreliable. A's only quoted demand is one LinkedIn commenter asking which vendor Stripe uses. A's brief admits this person was receiving gifts, not needing to send them.",
    "B names a budget-primed distribution channel: Zendesk Marketplace buyers already expect $500-$5,000+/yr for add-ons, and a source is given. A's Stripe App Marketplace channel has a sourced review gate but no evidence of buyer budget. A also cites a $150-$250 MQL cost from paid social.",
    "Both ideas face incumbents that already ship the core feature. B's compliance gates (SOC 2, HIPAA) can be avoided early by excluding regulated verticals and selling to small teams. A's per-kit landed cost ($30-75) and fulfillment risk apply to every single customer."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence rests on one LinkedIn commenter asking what vendor Stripe uses to send gifts. A's own brief says this person was receiving gifts, not needing to build or buy the workflow. The 'seed HN quote' it mentions is never reproduced or sourced, so it counts as missing. Nothing in A shows a SaaS founder willing to pay for triggered swag.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B's demand quotes come from family caregivers, not the support-team payer the idea targets, so neither brief shows a confirmed payer. B's '41% faster resolution / 47% higher first-contact resolution' figures appear without citations and were treated as missing. B wins mainly because it avoids A's physical-logistics burden and enterprise sales motion. It does not win on strong demand proof."
}
```
